title: IsoCLIP: Decomposing CLIP Projectors for Efficient Intra-modal Alignment

split.decision: Training-free. Public Caltech101 CoOp val queries (1649), train gallery (4128), seed 20261030. Hidden original eight-dataset evaluation: seven test/train retrieval sets and CUB all/all. Query sets disjoint; Caltech train gallery is public reference imagery, shared as required by the retrieval protocol. Opaque privately permuted ids and image ordering. All other datasets withheld.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 1 IsoCLIP OpenAI ViT-B/32 kt=150 kb=50; reproduced mean 45.359.

allowed_changes: The projector decomposition/filtering, feature postprocessing, similarity function and retrieval method may change on top of the fixed representation. Validation labels may select configurations but cannot become answers or lookup tables.
When retaining the supplied IsoCLIP projector, changing only iso_ktop=150 or iso_kbottom=50 does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Improve image-to-image retrieval by postprocessing the fixed pretrained CLIP ViT-B/32 representation.
The supplied CLIP ViT-B/32 encoder architecture, pretrained weights/buffers and released image decoding/RGB/resize/crop/normalization are fixed.
The supplied raw query/gallery images, self-match exclusion, full-gallery float32 AP/tie handling and equal-collection mean mAP remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not replace or fine-tune the encoder, introduce another pretrained model or extra training data, change encoder preprocessing, use answer lookups, change gallery membership/self-exclusion or alter the AP metric.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.

evidence.finding: The curated score rule fixes the frozen ViT-B/32 and prohibits extra training data.
The experiment analyzes and modifies the cross-modal projectors of a pretrained frozen CLIP representation for intra-modal retrieval.
The baseline extracts the unprojected frozen visual features, derives a new projector and computes retrieval similarities.
